title: RBAC role inheritance bug + KMS audit mismatch — urgent private deployment patch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Two enterprise Private customers reported unexpected elevated privileges for service accounts after a role change. Investigation found a bug in the RBAC role inheritance logic where revoked permissions in a parent role were not consistently propagated to nested role bindings on Private deployments that use our legacy role-merging path. Concurrently, audit logs emitted by the KMS integration showed mismatched request IDs and missing envelope IDs for ~12% of relevant events, preventing reliable forensics. Both issues together create unacceptable security and compliance risk for Private customers and require an urgent patch and coordinated rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:47 - Priya Rao (Customer Success): High-severity escalation from Soteria Health (SOC team). They observed a service account retaining old privileges after a role downgrade. Customer requested immediate mitigation and timeline.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Miguel Torres: Reproduced locally against private-vpc test infra. Root cause traced to the role-merge optimizer (role_merge_v2) skipping explicit deny propagation when a nested binding used a cached 'effective_roles' snapshot. Preparing a corrective patch to recompute effective_roles for affected binds at write-time.

2026-03-10 14:15 - Lin Chen (Security Eng): Discovered related KMS audit mismatch: envelope_id was conditionally omitted when request concurrency > 16 due to a race in async KMS client. This breaks audit correlation between RBAC changes and KMS key usage. Added deterministic write path to include envelope_id synchronously for RBAC-affecting requests as a temporary mitigation.
